## California Security Deposit Checklist

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

You can use a calm, evidence-first approach here. Since this is a California rental deposit dispute, the most useful next step is to gather records, ask for a written breakdown, and request the remaining deposit in writing.

## What to Gather Before You Reply

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg

- Lease agreement, including any addenda and move-out clauses
- Proof of the security deposit payment, showing **USD 1,800**
- Move-in inspection report, photos, and any emails about pre-existing carpet condition
- Move-out photos/videos with date stamps if available
- Your move-out notice and the date you returned keys: **2026-03-15**
- Any cleaning receipts, repair receipts, or contractor estimates you already have
- All landlord messages about the alleged carpet damage
- Your forwarding address and proof you provided it
- A copy of the landlord’s deposit accounting, if they already sent one

## Questions to Ask the Landlord

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/chat-square-text.svg

- What exact carpet damage is being claimed?
- Is the landlord treating this as ordinary wear and tear, cleaning, or actual repair?
- What portion of the **USD 900** is for carpet replacement versus cleaning or other charges?
- What documentation supports the charge, such as photos, invoices, or estimates?
- Was the carpet damaged beyond normal use, and where in the unit did it occur?
- When was the property inspected after move-out?
- If the carpet was replaced, was it fully replaced or partially repaired?
- What amount of the deposit is being returned now, and when will it be sent?

## Draft Email Requesting Itemized Explanation and Deposit Return

Subject: Request for Itemized Security Deposit Accounting and Return of Remaining Deposit

Hello [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I am writing about the security deposit for [property address]. I paid a security deposit of **USD 1,800** when I signed the lease on **2025-11-01**, and I moved out on **2026-03-15**.

You informed me that **USD 900** may be withheld for carpet damage. Please send me a written itemized explanation showing:
- each charge being withheld
- the specific reason for each charge
- any photos, invoices, estimates, or receipts supporting the charge
- whether the charge is for repair, replacement, or cleaning

If any part of the carpet charge is for ordinary wear and tear, I would appreciate clarification on how that was calculated. Please also return the undisputed portion of my deposit and confirm the mailing date for the remaining balance.

My forwarding address is:
[Your forwarding address]

Thank you for your prompt attention. I look forward to your written response.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your phone number]
[Your email address]

## Practical Next Step

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock.svg

- Send the email in writing and keep a copy.
- Save all photos, messages, and receipts in one folder.
- If the landlord responds with receipts or photos, compare them with your move-in and move-out records.

## Sources

- California Department of Consumer Affairs, tenant guidance: https://www.dca.ca.gov/publications/landlordbook/tenant-deposit.shtml
- California Civil Code, security deposit rules: https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&division=3.&title=5.&part=4.&chapter=2.&article=2
- California Courts Self-Help, housing and tenant resources: https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/landlords-tenants
